member.name: T:NaturalGasPipeline.Correlations.GeneralFlowEquation
member.summary:
General Flow Equation in USCS field units (Menon, Gas Pipeline Hydraulics):
Q = 38.77 · F · (Tb/Pb) · [ (P1² − e^s·P2²) / (G · Tf · Le · Z) ]^0.5 · D^2.5
with the transmission factor F = 2/√f (Darcy f) from any : - Colebrook-White, Haaland, Swamee-Jain, Churchill → "General Flow"; - or → "AGA"; - / → user F or f.
F depends on Re = 4·ṁ/(π·D·μ), which depends on Q: given N, Q and F are found by fixed-point iteration; given Q, F is direct. This is the same physics as (SI, exact constants); the field form is kept to reproduce published examples. The constant 38.77 is reproduced exactly by CED course P06-001, Example 12 (P1 = 1180.44 psig), see tests.

member.name: T:NaturalGasPipeline.Correlations.IGasFlowEquation
member.summary:
A steady-state, isothermal pipeline flow equation written as a relation between the standard flow Q and the pressure term
N = P1² − e^s · P2² (Pa²)
with the elevation parameter s and the equivalent length Le = L·(e^s − 1)/s already folded into . Both directions are required so that P1, P2, Q and D can all be solved for ().
To add an equation: implement this interface, state the source, the field units of its constants and its range of application, convert to those units only inside the implementation, and add tests against a published worked example.

member.name: T:NaturalGasPipeline.Correlations.PowerLawFlowEquation
member.summary:
Empirical flow equations of the common form (USCS field units):
Q = C · E · (Tb/Pb)^a · [ (P1² − e^s·P2²) / (G^b · Tf · Le · Z) ]^c · D^d
Q standard flow, ft³/day at (Tb, Pb) Tb, Tf °R Pb, P1, P2 psia Le miles D internal diameter, in G specific gravity (air = 1) E pipeline efficiency (explicit input; 1.0 for new pipe)
The friction factor is built into the constants (Weymouth: f ∝ D^(−1/3); Panhandle: f ∝ Re^(−n)). Constants from Menon, Gas Pipeline Hydraulics (2005), USCS forms; they reproduce exactly (0.01 psia) the Panhandle A, Panhandle B and Weymouth results of the CED Engineering course "Gas Pipeline Hydraulics" (P06-001), Example 11, and Arnold & Stewart Examples 6.2, 6.5 and 6.6a — see GasFlowEquationValidationTests.

member.name: T:System.Runtime.CompilerServices.ModuleInitializerAttribute
member.summary: Used to indicate to the compiler that a method should be called in its containing module's initializer.
member.remarks:
When one or more valid methods with this attribute are found in a compilation, the compiler will emit a module initializer which calls each of the attributed methods.
Certain requirements are imposed on any method targeted with this attribute: - The method must be `static`. - The method must be an ordinary member method, as opposed to a property accessor, constructor, local function, etc. - The method must be parameterless. - The method must return `void`. - The method must not be generic or be contained in a generic type. - The method's effective accessibility must be `internal` or `public`.
The specification for module initializers in the .NET runtime can be found here: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/design/specs/Ecma-335-Augments.md#module-initializer
